FOREWORD This lndian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 12 September 1989. after the draft finalized by the Cordage Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard has been revised in the light of the experience gained since its publication in 1980. In this revision, the following major changes have been carried out: a) Breaking load values after conditioning at -20�C for 24 hours have been modified, b) Test method for determining colour fastness has been modified, and c) New sampling clause has been added. This standard is mainly based on JSS: 4020-06, June 1981 `Cord Nylon' Defence, Government of India. issued by the Ministry of

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

POLYAMIDE CORD - SPECIFICATION ( First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes requirements for two varieties of plain twisted and braided polyamide cords for use in ammunition stores and packaging. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 MANUFACTURE 3.1 Yarn It shall be well twisted polyamide multifilament yarn of adequate tenacity to give specified cord strength.
NOTE -For identification of yarn see IS 667 : 1981.

3.2 Strands The strands shall consist of sufficient and equal number of yarns to form a cord. The twist in the strand shall be in the opposite direction to that of yarn. 3.3 Cord The finished cord shall be evenly twisted and as far as possible free from defects in yarn, strands and finish. The cord shall be free from weighting or loading substances. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The polyamide cord shall meet the physical requirements given in Table 1. 4.3 Coloor Fastness Requirement When the dyed polyamide cord is tested as per the method given in Annex B, the colour of the treated cord specimen shall compare favourably with that of untreated cord specimen and there shall be no appreciable change in the colour of the soap solution. , 5 PACKING 5.1 Unless otherwise specified in the contract or order, the cord shall be packed as per the procedure given in 5.1.1. 5.1.1 Each hank/cheese shall be wrapped in polyethylene film, and then a suitable number of such hanks/cheeses shall be wrapped together in another layer of polyethylene film. Finally the package shall be covered with a layer of hessian cloth conforming to Type I of IS 28 18 ( Part 2 ) : 1971 and stitched. 6 MARKING 6.1 Each package shall bear the following information suitably marked: a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; b) Name of the material and variety number; c) Net quantity in the package both in m and in kg; d) Date of Manufacture; and e) Any other information required by the buyer. 1

IS 9536 : 1989 7 SAMPLING 7.1 Lot The quantity of cords of the same variety manufactured under similar conditions and delivered to a buyer against a despatch note shall constitute a lot. 7.2 Sample Size Sampling shall be as represeptative as possible of the lot subjected to the measurements and tests. Draw the sample pack? + at random at the rate shbwn by the following Pormulti s = 0'4JN where S is the sample size of the packages of cords and N is the size of the lot expressed as the number of packages. When S as calculated is not a whole number, round off the value obtained to give a whole number in accordance with the requirements of IS 2 : 1960. In cases where S is less than one, draw one sample package. 7.3 The number of packages selected according to 7.2 shall be tested for linear density, diameter and breaking load in the standard atmosphere. For the remaining characteristics, namely breaking load after conditioning at - 2O"C, pH of aqueous extract, ash content, water soluble chlorides, water soluble sulphates and colour fastness the number of packages to be tested shall be 2 selected in 7.2. In case the sample size as selected in 7.2 is one package only then all the tests shall be carried out on test specimens drawn from ope sample package only. 7.4.1 For each test adequate amount of cord sample shall be selected from each package to be tested as per 7.3. 7.4 Criteria for Conf@r@y The lot shall be considered to be conforming to the requirements of this standard if none of the packages tested according to 7.3 fail to meet the spewed requiqments.

ANNEX

B

( Clause 4.3 )
METHOD FOR

DETERMINATION OF COLOUR FASTNESS TO WASHING

B-l PRINCIPLE B-l.1 A specimen of cord is dipped in a soap solution under specified conditions of time and temperature and the cord is stirred from time to time manually or by applying mechanical means.

( stainless steel ) container and add required amount of soap solution previously heated to 60 rt 2"C, to give a liquor ratio 50 : 1. Treat the specimen at the temperature for 15 minutes and while treating the specimen shall be stirred continously through mechanical means or manually. B-4.2 Remove the test specimen and rinse it in cold running tap water for 10 minutes and squeeze it and dry it by hanging it in air at a temperature not exceeding 60�C. B-4.3 Assess the change in colour of the specimen along with an untreated test specimen drawn from the sample package and also assess the change in colour of the soap solution. B-5 TEST REPORT ES.1 Report whether the colour of the treated cord spectmen compares favourably wtth that of un-treated cord specimen and whether any appreciable change in the colour of the soap solution is noticed.

B-2 REAGENTS
B-2.1 Soap Solution

Soap solution shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 3361 : 1979. B-3 TEST SPECIMEN B-3.1 Two 50 cm test length of polyamide cord selected from a package. One for treating with soap solution and the other for comparing with the treated specimen. B-4 PROCEDURE
B-4.1 Place the test specimen in non-corrodible

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BJS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
